newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt cancels corn and soybean tenders.
newsitem.headline: Egypt cancels corn and soybean tenders.

text.p: Egypt has cancelled a tender for 30,000 tonnes of corn after a government decree was issued this month requiring proof that grain imports were not genetically-altered, an official said on Wednesday.

The official told Reuters the state Holding Company for Food Industries also cancelled a tender for 30,000 tonnes of soybeans because it had received only one offer, making price comparison impossible.

"We cancelled the tenders, both of them. We have cancelled the tenders yesterday," said the official, who declined to be named. "We received only one offer for soya and there was no opportunity to compare."

The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company had tendered for yellow corn for arrival in the second half of September and/or the second half of October and of U.S. or Argentine origin. The soybean tender, for any origin material, required arrival in the first half of October and/or the first half of November. The deadline for the bids was July 22.
The official said the decision was taken to cancel because of uncertainty because the delivery fell after October 1.
Egypt's health ministry issued the decree requiring imported commodities meant for human consumption to have a certificate saying they were not genetically altered. It was dated July 1.
A memorandum, obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, requested the health minister to delay implementing the decree until October and asking him to let in all grain shipments, except for "suspect soybeans".
Asked if he planned to enter the market before October, the official said: "It depends. We always tender for soya and corn according to our requirements."
